## 2024-07-10 - [Gnuplot Script Injection & Insecure Temp Files]
**Vulnerability:** Gnuplot script files (`.plt`) were generated by performing blind string replacements for variables like title or filename without proper escaping, leading to OS command injection via Gnuplot's `!` shell execution capability. Additionally, predictable, shared temporary directories were used without cleanup, leading to disk space leakage and potential cross-user file manipulation.
**Learning:** External script generation tools (like Gnuplot or Pandoc) can be vectors for command injection if they have shell execution abilities. Simply inserting unsanitized user strings into script files is extremely dangerous. Predictable hardcoded temp paths also allow concurrent executions to overwrite each other's data.
**Prevention:** Always escape user input when injecting into script files. Use ephemeral UUID-based directories created via `System.tmp_dir!()` for processing, and ensure `try/after` blocks are strictly implemented to clean up these temporary directories once script execution or processing completes.
